correctness.rationale: A complete normalized proof derives the annular transform by subtraction; establishes E_nu strictly increasing from exact Bessel recurrences for nu>=1; deduces strict endpoint dominance and, at every root, a derivative with the fixed sign of J_(nu-1); proves uniqueness, simplicity, absence below first bracket, analytic motion, both endpoint limits, and uniform root counts. The dimension-one factorization is exhaustive and proves double zeros only at explicit rational resonances. The checker independently evaluated 112 root instances and 12 integrals, but no finite computation is relied on for infinite assertions.

originality.rationale: The previously established annulus Fourier amplitude and classical Bessel interlacing do not themselves yield a root census for J_nu(t) - r^nu J_nu(rt). The derived strict Bessel energy identity provides new implication-level control of cancellation and derivative orientation, giving all radii and all dimensions >=2 together with a sharp dimension-one counterphenomenon. The self-review includes complete accessible full text for the most relevant sources, but unindexed optical literature may contain a similar result.
residual_risks: An obscure older annular-optics paper or a special-function inequalities monograph may have proved equivalent scaled-Bessel interlacing without discoverable keywords.
Abstract-level derivative and generalized-order-interlacing sources are not sufficient to rule out uninspected developments; their available statements concern different combinations.
The finding has only self-review, not external independent mathematical validation.

value.rationale: Annular diffraction nulls are the native observable of concentric apertures. A full dimension-uniform one-root-per-Bessel-gap census, regularity of all nodal spheres, analytic ball-to-sphere interpolation, and a sharp one-dimensional resonance contrast are natural structural outputs with use for Fourier-null geometry and aperture design; not just a routine recurrence or a numerical table.
